memory_update.text: Keep DDOG as the reference leader for observability plus cloud security; do not let it crowd out the underfollowed lane in later layers.
Add FROG to the underfollowed software-supply-chain lane; key validation is whether ML model governance and security products become material ARR contributors.
Add PD as a small-cap AI/cloud operations automation candidate; key validation is whether AIOps and agentic operations improve growth and retention.
Add TENB as an exposure-management/cloud-identity candidate; key validation is whether Tenable One, cloud security, identity exposure, and AI exposure modules drive platform expansion.

Pure-play public machine-identity and secrets-management exposure remains sparse; later passes should test whether private/acquired leaders such as Venafi/DigiCert-style assets create public-market second-order beneficiaries through partners, integrators, or adjacent vendors.

node: Cloud security, machine identity, observability, infrastructure automation, data governance, and workload orchestration software
summary: Layer 1B expands the software-side cloud complexity chokepoint. The reference lane is Datadog as the visible observability/security consolidator. The underfollowed lane favors smaller public software companies one step away from obvious AI software hype: JFrog for software/ML supply-chain control, PagerDuty for incident automation and AI operations, and Tenable for cloud/identity/exposure management. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. Key unresolved issue: this node is commercially attractive but less physically supply-constrained than semiconductor or power chokepoints, so later layers must prove pricing power, net retention, free cash flow durability, and whether AI/cloud complexity is creating incremental spend rather than vendor re-labeling.
